title: No Fair Lunch: A Causal Perspective on Dataset Bias in Machine Learning for Medical Imaging

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing prevalence disparities using causal directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) to model how patient race and disparate healthcare access can spuriously correlate with disease prevalence in datasets (e.g., skin lesion biopsies).

Using causal graphs to evaluate both fair prevalence disparities (e.g., age as a risk factor for Alzheimer's) and annotation disparities (e.g., age-dependent differential diagnosis criteria for osteoporosis).
Applying causal diagrams to model fair presentation disparities caused by natural physiological differences, such as variations in breast density between sexes affecting mammogram features.

Modeling unfair presentation disparities across different patient locations using causal graphs to illustrate the impact of inconsistent referral policies, varying scanner artifacts, and differing diagnostic workflows.
Using causal graphs to conceptualize annotation disparities where automated labels generated from radiology reports vary in quality depending on the native language of the reports.
